script.title: Chapter 4: The Fishermen of the Pepper Coast

panels.description: Wide, full page width. A storm-spent sea under a flat grey sky, long heavy swells breaking on a shallow curve of beach. Black rock outcrops break the sand. Small in the foam, Nagoji is thrown face down onto the beach, one arm flung out. Floating timber in the surf behind him. No other people anywhere. No irons, manacles, chain or collar on him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: When the sea finally spat me out, it did so without ceremony.

panels.description: Ground level, tight. Nagoji's hands dug into coarse wet grit: the fingers wrapped in soaked, filthy bandage, the heels of the palms bare and raw with rope burn, the wrist bandages sodden and slipping. His left forearm is crusted with wet sand; no mark on it is readable yet. The retreating surf drags at his legs in the background. He is in the captivity rags, sodden: torn ochre sleeveless tunic, ripped open down the front, cream dhoti. Two loops of rope are still knotted across his chest under the armpits, well clear of the neck, the frayed free end trailing into the foam. Raw chafe rings at the ankles where iron once bit. No ankle irons, no manacles, no chain, no neck collar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Breathing was a battle. Each time I drew in air it brought more salt, more pain.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji's face, cheek pressed to wet sand, one eye half open, long curly black hair plastered across it. Thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN (faint stubble shadow at most, no beard), small gold ear stud, no turban. A thin sheet of wave washes over his shoulder and back. His left arm is out of frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My limbs felt like they belonged to someone else, a man made of lead and bruises.

panels.description: Full width, bottom strip. Same low angle along the sand, but the tide line has moved and the light has shifted: time has passed. At the far edge of the panel, three pairs of bare brown feet are approaching over the sand, leaving prints. We see no more of them than that.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sea was no longer alone.

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: ...alive...

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: Look at his hands...

copy.speaker: VOICE (off)
copy.text: See the brand on his arm.

panels.description: Nagoji's point of view, flat on his back, looking straight up. A lowering grey sky, the colour of stale rice water. Three faces close the frame around it like a ring, framed by beards and damp hair, sun-and-salt brown skin. Faces, hair and beards only in this panel; the costumes are established in 2.4. Establish the three faces now and hold them for the chapter. **FISHERMAN**: forties, the leader, broad face, short grizzled beard, strong white teeth, the edge of a white cotton cloth on his LEFT shoulder. **YOUNG FISHERMAN**: twenties, slim face, thin black beard, quick eyes, a cloth tied round his head as a headband. **WARY FISHERMAN**: older and gaunt, long grey-streaked beard, the coil of a net on his shoulder, leaning in least, already half turned away.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They were not Portuguese.

panels.description: The Fisherman (short grizzled beard, shoulder cloth) pushes Nagoji's hair back from his forehead with rough fingers. Nagoji flinches, one bandaged hand half rising to guard his face. Habit, not fear. The rope loops are still across his chest; his left forearm stays sand-caked, no mark readable. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Easy, *bhau*. You are on land now.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: *Bhau.* Brother, in Konkani. Near enough to my Marathi.

panels.description: Tight. A clay pot pressed to Nagoji's cracked lips, water spilling down his clean-shaven chin and moustache. No beard.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Water.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first swallow burned. The second soothed.

panels.description: Wide, from just behind Nagoji's left shoulder as he props himself on his left elbow and looks past the men; his left forearm lies flat on the sand, inner side down. In the middle ground the three fishermen stand at full figure, so their costume reads; hold it for the chapter. All barefoot, lungis hitched up to the thigh, short sleeveless vests clinging wet. FISHERMAN: stocky, faded madder-red lungi, cream vest, white cotton cloth over his LEFT shoulder. YOUNG FISHERMAN: slim, indigo lungi, faded blue vest, cloth headband, sliding a short fishing knife back into his waist-knot; beside Nagoji on the sand lie the rope loops he has just cut away. WARY FISHERMAN: gaunt, undyed off-white lungi, dark brown vest, a coiled net over one shoulder. Beyond them: the shallow curve of beach, black rock, a line of coconut palms with fronds bent in the wind. On the sand to the right, the broken carcass of a ship's boat, planks scattered. Farther along the shore, half hidden in spray, the same black, high-sided ship from chapters 2 and 3, carved stern castle, mainmast snapped, heeled over and cracked open on a reef offshore. Timber bobbing in the surf. From here on, no rope on Nagoji, and no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I recognised the curve of a Portuguese hull.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Nagoji's point of view along the surf line, left to right: foam, floating planks, a torn scrap of sail. No human figure anywhere, in the water or on the sand. At most, a sliver of Nagoji's cheek and eye at the left edge of the foreground.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No bodies. Not that I could see.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Perhaps the sea had decided it had eaten enough men for one day.

panels.description: Wide. Nagoji half sitting, centre, the torn ochre tunic hanging open over raw rope burns on his chest; no rope on him. The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) kneels at Nagoji's RIGHT and turns up his right hand: the bandage wraps only the fingers, and the heel of the palm is bare, hard with rein and sword calluses and raw with fresh rope burn. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) kneels at Nagoji's LEFT, turns the left forearm over and scrapes a crust of wet sand off its inner side with his thumb, just above the slipping wrist bandage. What he uncovers is not yet readable at this distance. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <He has soldier's calluses. Not a clerk. Not a merchant.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Look at this.>

panels.description: Insert, tight, generated as its own close-up rather than cropped from a wider frame. The Portuguese brand on the inner side of Nagoji's LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist: a short row of raised, ridged burn scars, puckered and angry, crude marks blurred past reading. No legible letters, no numerals, no cross. The Fisherman's sandy thumb at the edge of frame, wet sand just scraped from around the mark. The soaked edge of the wrist bandage below it.
The Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net on shoulder) stands apart, ankle-deep at the tide line, glancing up the coast toward the wreck and then back at the others. He wants to be anywhere else.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They argued in Malayalam. I could not follow a word. I did not need to.

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Kill him. Why bring trouble to the village?>

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN
copy.text: <The Portuguese will send men for their ship. Better the sea finishes its work.>

panels.description: The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth), still crouched at Nagoji's side, snorts and turns his head to the Wary Fisherman. The posture of a man haggling at a fish market.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <The Portuguese and the Dutch ask questions anyway.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <You think leaving one marata on the sand will satisfy either of them?>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <We might as well gain something.>

panels.description: The Fisherman turns back to Nagoji and leans in, close. The look of a man doing sums. Nagoji meets his eyes. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: WARY FISHERMAN (off)
copy.text: <What? He is half dead.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: <Half is still half.>

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You fought them, yes?

panels.description: Wide, resetting the geography with every figure at full scale. Nagoji up on one elbow on the sand, water still running from his hair. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) crouched at his side; the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) standing over them; the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) a few paces off, already turned toward the palms. The wreck in the surf behind. Nagoji's voice is a rasp but his eyes are steady. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes. On the Deccan roads. Near their forts.

panels.description: The Fisherman nods once, as if a calculation has come out right, and jerks his chin south down the coast. The line of palms runs away into haze.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Our king to the south fights them too. And the other pale ones from the north, the Dutch.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: He sharpens his teeth for them.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: A man who has seen Portuguese dungeons and still breathes may be useful.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji. Something wakes behind the exhaustion. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache, gold ear stud.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: King. Teeth. Dutch. The words caught like hooks.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Travancore.

panels.description: Two-shot. The Fisherman's brows go up. Nagoji, still propped on one elbow, back straight, chin lifted, shoulders squared despite the exhaustion. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You know the name.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I know they have not yet learned to kneel when a foreign flag flies.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That is enough.

panels.description: Full width. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) grins, teeth white against weathered skin, as he takes Nagoji's shoulders; the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) takes his legs; the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) is already walking ahead, scanning the shore. In the foreground, a small sand crab sidles out of the way. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard; no irons, manacles, chain or collar.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: You see, he has a tongue as well as scars.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Come, *bhau*. Before the crabs claim you.

panels.description: Wide, high angle from up among the first coconut palms, looking back down the slope toward the sea. The carry party climbs toward us: the Wary Fisherman (off-white lungi, net) leading, the Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) carrying Nagoji's shoulders, the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) his legs. Nagoji slung between them, head tipped back, eyes on the fronds. Behind and below them: the empty beach, the ship's boat lying untouched on the sand, and the wreck small and far off on its reef. Nobody is stripping it. No irons or chains on Nagoji.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The smell of earth instead of salt.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: After the dungeon and the storm, these small things felt like gifts.

panels.description: Wide. The village beyond the palms: narrow paths between wet paddy, low houses of mud and red laterite stone with palm-thatch roofs. Children stare from doorways. Village women in plain mundu with an upper cloth draped over both shoulders, modestly covered, water pots on their hips, have stopped on the path. In the foreground, a small girl whispers to the child beside her, eyes on Nagoji, the dripping stranger carried between the fishermen in the middle distance.

copy.speaker: GIRL
copy.text: <Portuguese.>

panels.description: The Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband), carrying Nagoji's legs, turns his head sharply toward the girl. The girl shrinks back. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) holds Nagoji's shoulders at the far end. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <No. Look at his eyes. Look at his mark.>

copy.speaker: YOUNG FISHERMAN
copy.text: <This one is enemy of the Portuguese.>

panels.description: A low house at the edge of the village. The Woman steps out of the doorway, wiping her hands on her cloth: heavy-set, in her fifties, hair in a loose low knot heavily streaked with grey, betel-stained lips, no gold, no walking stick, coarse undyed cotton worn sari-fashion with the end drawn over both shoulders, no fitted blouse. One frozen moment: a faint betel-stained half-smile at the corner of her mouth, her gaze fixed on the brand. Nagoji, held between the carriers, has his LEFT forearm turned toward camera across his body so the brand on its inner side shows; the torn tunic hangs open over the raw rope burns on his chest. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) beside her, mid-gesture, talking. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: WOMAN
copy.text: <Bring him in.>

copy.speaker: WOMAN
copy.text: <If he dies, burn him quietly. Otherwise, send word to the *kapitan*.>

panels.description: Interior, cool and dim. Packed earth floor swept smooth; smoke from a small hearth curling up toward a hole in the thatch. Nagoji on a woven mat, the salt-stiff tunic peeled off and set aside, the cream dhoti left on him; rope burns across his chest; the brand on his left inner forearm. The Woman (grey-streaked low knot, undyed cotton) washes him with a cloth and a clay basin, brisk rather than gentle. She has unwound the bandage from one hand. Frame it so his fingers are turned away from us or lost in her shadow: we read the damage only in her face, her mouth pulled tight. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) squats at the mat's edge. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She asks what they did to you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Asked questions.

panels.description: The Woman (grey-streaked low knot, undyed cotton) clicks her tongue and wrings the cloth hard into the basin, speaking fast and sharp at no one in particular. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) relays it with half a smile. Nagoji on the mat in the foreground.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She says keep your stories for the *kapitan*.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: She does not need to hear them to know what kind of men they are.

panels.description: A boy in the doorway, backlit by grey daylight, panting, one hand on the frame, talking fast. The Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth) and the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) exchange a look across the room.

copy.speaker: BOY
copy.text: ... *kapitan* ... *kapitan* ...

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: So. I was not the first piece of foreign wreckage to wash up in their nets.

panels.description: The Fisherman (red lungi), crouched by the mat, adjusts the white cotton cloth on his own left shoulder (the one established in 2.1), voice low. Nagoji on the mat, looking up at him. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: Rest. When the *kapitan* comes, speak carefully.

copy.speaker: FISHERMAN
copy.text: He works for men who have long arms.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Storms on land were different from storms at sea. They did not roar and crash; they crept in on quiet feet, through conversations and calculations.

panels.description: Full-width tier, not a narrow strip. Nagoji's eyes closed, hearth light on his face. Behind him, out of focus, the Fisherman and the Young Fisherman are turning their heads toward the door, straightening, and a broad shadow falls across the swept floor. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had escaped the Portuguese dungeon and the drowning ship by chance and stubbornness.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If I was to survive whatever came next, I would need more than that.

panels.description: Large, about the bottom 40 percent of the page. Camera low, from beside Nagoji's mat, looking up. The *kapitan* has stepped a pace inside so his face is in the room: three-quarter view with HIS OWN (anatomical) left cheek toward camera, lit warm by the hearth; the scar runs from that left ear to the corner of his jaw. Grey daylight from the doorway only rims his shoulders. Shorter than the fishermen but broader: the Young Fisherman (indigo lungi, headband) stands just behind him, half a head taller, drawing back with respect beside the Fisherman (red lungi, shoulder cloth). White turban, short grey-flecked beard, pale vest over a white mundu. No coat (the coat arrives in chapter 6). He says nothing. A slow, appraising look moves over the brand, the hands, the shoulders; Nagoji's left forearm lies on the mat, inner side up, toward him. Nagoji, on the mat in the foreground, has opened his eyes and is looking straight back. Nagoji: clean-shaven chin, no beard, thick moustache; no irons or chains.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His eyes moved over me the way a horse trader's eyes move over new stock.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen that look before, in market squares where men were sold.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In that silence, I was being weighed.

frames.review_note: v02 is clean. It is a wide storm-grey beach with black rock outcrops and timber in the surf. Nagoji lies small and face down in the foam with his arms flung out and bandaged wrists, and a frayed rope end trails from him, which matches 1.2. There are no irons, chain or collar, and plenty of empty sky for the caption. v01 is not acceptable. It crops Nagoji large in the foreground rather than small in the foam, which breaks the wide establishing beat. It also leaves his hands and wrists unbandaged, which contradicts the bandaged fingers in 1.2.

v04 fits the script beat best: a ground-level shot tight on both bandaged hands clawed into wet grit. The fingers are wrapped and the backs of the hands and wrists are raw red. The left forearm (image right) is heavily crusted with sand and shows no readable mark. The torn ochre tunic hangs open, a rope loop crosses the chest, and the free end trails off into the foam at right. His knees and dhoti sit in the retreating surf. There are no irons, collar, painted text or blood. The face is cropped at the nose, so the eyes stay for 1.3's close-up. What shows matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven stubbled chin, gold ear stud, loose curly hair. Minor flaws: each hand shows only four digits, but one finger reads as buried in the grit, which suits 'dug into' the sand. Only one rope loop is visible where the script asks for two, and he is braced on straight arms rather than slumped. The caption fits the clear sky at top right (about x 0.72-1.0, y 0-0.18). Backup v03 has cleaner five-digit hands and correct identity. Its weaknesses are framing and sequence: it is a wider medium shot, not tight on the hands, and it shows his full face alert and looking off. That pre-empts 1.3's close-up of his cheek pressed to the sand with one eye half open.

Minor only. The right side of the moustache droops down toward the sand instead of curling up, which reads as wet hair pressed flat, not a beard. The cheek and jaw are clean and the chin is pressed into the sand. The shoulder and back mass is soft but reads as a man lying face down. The rope loops on the torso sit on the shoulder and ribs, well clear of the neck, which matches 1.2. The caption fits over the grey sky and distant surf at the top left, clear of the face.

In v01 the lower legs run up to about knee height at the top edge, behind where the balloons sit. Nothing else of the men shows. The light shifts to a low sun breaking under grey storm cloud, which still sits well beside the grey sky of 2.1. Otherwise it matches the beat: the same low angle along the sand, a moved tide line, and three pairs of bare brown feet walking in from the right edge and leaving a trail of prints. Toe counts and anatomy are sound, and the open sky at left and centre takes the caption and the off-panel voices. Rejected: v02 has only five feet, and the legs are cut off by a hard horizontal line under the balloon. v03 has five disembodied feet ending at the ankle in mid-air. v04 shows only two pairs of legs. v06 shows four feet stacked in a column with no legs. v05 is the backup: three sound pairs of feet, but they stand still in the shallows rather than approaching with a trail of prints, and there is no horizon or sky to show the time shift.

v03 is clean. It is Nagoji's point of view looking up into a grey sky, and the three faces ring the frame. The Fisherman has a short grizzled beard, white teeth and the white cloth on his LEFT shoulder. The Young Fisherman is inverted at the top, with a headband, a thin black beard and a blue cloth over one bare shoulder. The Wary Fisherman has a long grey-streaked beard and a net coil, and his eyes are turned away. There is no painted text. Open sky at the top left and the bottom centre has room for the caption. v02 is nearly identical, but the Young Fisherman wears a blue sleeveless vest over both shoulders. That contradicts the chapter costume (bare-chested, no vests), so it is not used as backup.

v04 is acceptable. The Fisherman is bare-chested, with a short grizzled beard, a red lungi and a white cloth hanging from his left shoulder. He pushes Nagoji's hair back. Nagoji flinches, with a bandaged hand half raised to his face. The rope loops are across his chest and no forearm mark is readable. Nagoji has a thick moustache, a clean-shaven chin with faint stubble and a gold ear stud. The setting is the same stormy beach with black rocks. Minor: Nagoji's moustache ends droop more than curl. His raised arm is folded sharply and carries two bandage bands, but it reads correctly. Room for the speech balloon: open sky at the top right or top left. Room for the caption: low-detail cream dhoti at the bottom left. v03 is not acceptable because the Fisherman wears a cream sleeveless vest (chapter costume is bare-chested, no vests).

v02 is acceptable. Water pours from a clay pot into Nagoji's mouth and runs down his clean-shaven chin. His moustache and gold stud match the sheet, rope burns show on his chest, and the background is empty surf. A fisherman's brown arm and cream vest are visible, and the second hand under the pot is plausible. The framing is a medium close-up rather than truly tight, and the pot pours at his lips rather than being pressed to them. That is acceptable. No rope is visible on the chest, which fits because 2.4 shows the rope already cut away. Rejected v01: Portuguese soldiers in morions stand in the background with a fort, the pot is held by a man in a European doublet and belt (the beat is 'They were not Portuguese'), and the brand is shown on his forearm too early.

v05 is acceptable and is the only candidate where the fishermen are bare-chested. The view is from behind Nagoji's left shoulder: he is propped on his left elbow, the forearm lies flat on the sand, and the gold ear stud shows. There is no rope or iron on him, and the cut rope loops lie beside him. The Fisherman wears a red lungi with a white cloth on his LEFT shoulder. The Young Fisherman wears an indigo lungi, a blue shoulder cloth and a headband, and slides a knife into his waist-knot. The Wary Fisherman wears an off-white lungi, a brown shoulder cloth and a net. Behind them are black rocks and palms, the broken ship's boat with scattered planks on the right, and the dismasted black ship heeled over on the reef. There is no painted text. Minor issues: (1) Nagoji's right hand, half hidden under his chest, is unbandaged. (2) The upper side of his left forearm has a whitish lacy crust that reads as salt or sand, not letters or a brand. (3) The Fisherman's beard is thinner than in 2.1 and 2.2. Large open storm sky at the top right has room for the caption. v04 is not acceptable because all three fishermen wear sleeveless vests.

v01 is clean. It is a narrow surf-line strip of foam, floating planks and a torn scrap of sail on a spar, with black rocks at right matching the rest of the page. No human figure appears anywhere, and two clear sky areas take the two captions. Rejected v02: the bottom third of the frame is a blank white area, so the image is broken.

Minor only. Nagoji's left foot has a hand-style bandage with toes showing. The Young Fisherman's indigo lungi hangs full length instead of being hitched to the thigh, and his blue cloth drapes across much of his torso. The sky for lettering is a fairly shallow band: top-left above the wreck, and top centre-right above the palms. Nagoji is on-model: clean-shaven chin, thick moustache, gold stud, rope burns, no rope. The Young Fisherman holds the right hand at Nagoji's right, and the Fisherman scrapes sand from the left forearm at Nagoji's left. The forearm mark cannot be read. v06 is almost the same frame but puts both fishermen in sleeveless vests, which breaks the bare-chested costume rule, so there is no backup.

Clean. This is a real tight insert, not a crop. The brand on the inner forearm, above the soaked wrist bandage, is a puckered patch of ridged scar tissue with no legible letters, numerals or cross, and no blood. The Fisherman's sandy thumb is scraping wet sand at the left edge. The ochre tunic, cream dhoti and grey surf behind match 3.1. No lettering needed.

Minor. He stands calf to knee deep in the surf rather than ankle-deep. The other men are not shown, which suits 'stands apart'. The Wary Fisherman is gaunt and bare-chested, with a long grey-streaked beard, an off-white lungi, a dark brown cloth and the net over his shoulder. He glances up toward the wreck. The large sky gives plenty of room for the caption and two balloons. v06 puts him in a brown sleeveless vest, against the no-vest rule, so there is no backup.

Fix landed. A pixel diff against v07 shows only Nagoji's hands changed. In v08 every finger on both hands is wrapped in bandage, and the fingers read as separate wrapped digits. The only bare skin is a speck at one fingertip on his left hand, which is negligible. Nothing else got worse: same beach, sky, wreck and figures as v07. The Fisherman is bare-chested in a red lungi with a white shoulder cloth, crouched and turned toward the Wary Fisherman with a haggling open hand. The Wary Fisherman stands at the tide line in an off-white lungi with a net on his shoulder. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear ornament, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, rope burns on chest. There is no painted text, no blood and no anachronism. The tan blotch on the bandage is sand or dirt, not red. The large overcast sky across the top gives room for all three Fisherman balloons. Minor continuity note, not a reason to reject: the wraps now run further up both forearms than the bible's finger wraps with a bare palm heel (3.1). The brand on the inner left forearm is not in view here anyway.

Minor. Nagoji's hand bandages carry muted brown stains; they read as dirt but could be taken for old blood. The bandage style matches 3.4 but not 3.1. The Fisherman's white cloth hangs from his right shoulder instead of his left. The rock at the left edge looks somewhat like masonry. The beat works: the Fisherman leans in close with his hand at his chin, doing sums, and Nagoji meets his eyes. Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, thick moustache and gold stud. The off-panel Wary Fisherman's tail goes to the left frame edge, consistent with where he stood in 3.4. There is clear sky across the top for three balloons. v04 puts the Fisherman in a vest, so there is no backup.

v08 is clean. It is wide, with Nagoji up on one elbow (moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold stud, ochre rags, bandaged hands, no irons). The Fisherman crouches in a red lungi with a shoulder cloth, the Young Fisherman stands in an indigo lungi and headband, and the Wary Fisherman holds the net and looks toward the palms, with the wreck in the surf behind. The open grey sky at top centre takes the single balloon. Small note: the Young Fisherman also wears a small ear stud. v07 is not an acceptable backup because all three fishermen wear knitted singlets or tank tops, which are anachronistic and are the reason for this chapter's vest-removal pass.

Acceptable. The bare-chested Fisherman in a red lungi with a white shoulder cloth directs south down a palm-lined coast fading into haze. Nagoji is seen from behind at left (curly hair, gold stud, ochre rag). The open cloudy sky on the right easily holds three balloons. Minor staging drift: the Fisherman is standing and points with his arm instead of jerking his chin, while he crouches in 4.1 and 4.4. The beat still reads. v06 is not an acceptable backup because of the anachronistic cream singlet.

Minor drift only. v05 is the r9 pick (v04) with the hand bandages restored, which matches 4.1, 4.4 and page 3.
